subject: Re: DPA clarifications — controller/processor and breach notice
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orion-payments.com>, Priya Rao <priya@orion-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA follow-up / post-demo recap

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the privacy items we promised to follow up on: 

1) Roles: You asked whether Orion would be classified as the controller and Redwood as the processor in the standard DPA.
2) Subprocessors: You want a current list of subprocessors and whether Redwood will notify you of additions.
3) Breach notice: You asked for our breach-notification SLA (you mentioned 72 hours as a target).
4) Data residency: You mentioned a preference for eu-west-1 for payment data; requested confirmation of available regions.
5) Data handling: Clarify PII treatment, retention windows, and logging controls (what we log and for how long).

Next steps from our side: Dylan will provide a brief technical note on logging and retention, and Marissa will coordinate legal responses and send the DPA v2 (clean copy) + subprocessors list. I can also send a one-page procurement checklist if useful. 

Could you confirm which items are the highest priority for procurement (e.g., breach notice window vs. residency) and whether you need a formal NDA before we share the SOC 2 report?

Attaching a short meeting notes stub.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachment: 20270510-meeting-notes.txt (meeting notes, 1 page)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orion-payments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@orion-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up / post-demo recap

Thanks Ben — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Correct: Orion Payments will be the controller for customer payment data; Redwood will be the processor. We need that reflected in the DPA language.
- Subprocessors: please send your current list and confirm whether you provide 30 days notice prior to onboarding new subprocessors (or if you require customer-level opt-out).
- Breach notice: our security team requires 72 hours initial notice for incidents that materially affect customer data. Can Redwood commit to a 72-hour initial notification window?
- Data residency: we need confirmation that Redwood can ensure that onboarding for our account is limited to eu-west-1 for production payment workloads.
- SOC 2: please share SOC 2 Type II evidence (we can sign an NDA if needed).

Procurement timeline: we are aiming to be contract-executed by end of May; legal will prioritize the DPA review if we get a clean copy and subprocessors list this week.

Alex Johnson
Head of Security & Compliance | Orion Payments
alex.johnson@orion-payments.com | +44 20 7946 0821

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@orion-payments.com>, Priya Rao <priya@orion-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA follow-up / post-demo recap

Hi Alex — thanks, that helps. High-level answers below; Marissa and Dylan are cc'd to add details and formal language. We are happy to move quickly on this.

- Controller/Processor: Redwood's standard position is to act as a processor when processing customer data on behalf of customers; the enclosed DPA v2 uses processor language but we can mark the relevant clauses explicitly for your legal team.
- Subprocessors: current list attached (subprocessors_list_202705.csv). Redwood publishes a list of subprocessors and provides advance notice of changes; the standard notice window is 30 days. If you require a customer-specific approval flow we can discuss, but that typically triggers contract-level exceptions.
- Breach notice: Redwood aims to provide initial breach notification within 72 hours where feasible; the DPA currently commits to "prompt notification" and we can propose a 72-hour SLA for consensus. Marissa, legal — can confirm.
- Data residency: we support region scoping at account level and can restrict production workloads to eu-west-1; we'll need to capture this in the contract and provisioning checklist.
- SOC 2: we can share SOC 2 Type II on an NDA. Link to request form: https://redwood-internal.s3.amazonaws.com/soc2-report-request-form

Next steps: 
1) Marissa to share annotated DPA v2 (clean copy) and confirm breach-notice SLA language.
2) Dylan to send a short note on logging retention and what telemetry we retain by default.
3) If you confirm residency requirement now, I'll flag the account provisioning to restrict to eu-west-1.

Attaching: DPA_v2_Redwood.pdf (clean copy), subprocessors_list_202705.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: DPA follow-up / post-demo recap (internal)

Ben — thanks for looping me in. I'll prepare a marked-up DPA with explicit processor/controller language and propose a 72-hour initial notification clause. Also will confirm the subprocessors notice language (30 days) and escalate any ask for customer-specific approval to legal leadership.

I'll wait for Dylan's logging/retention note and then send the package to Alex/Priya with an ask to confirm residency. If they need SOC 2 now, please have them sign the NDA form linked; we can provision the report once it's executed.

-Marissa
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
